title: SRE on-call scratchpad - 2026-03-21
content:
Morning oncall notes - 2026-03-21

Summary:
- PagerDuty: 2 pages overnight (KV cache evictions, worker OOMs). Both paged at ~02:10 and ~03:05 UTC.
- Services impacted: inference-worker (short tail latency spikes), cache-service (higher miss rate).
- Current status: mitigations applied, monitoring steady. Postmortem in progress for cache evictions.

Timeline / actions taken:
- 02:05 UTC: alert SRE-High - cache-service evictions spike (error rate -> 8% in 5m).
  - Command run: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/cache-service (temporary) -> no immediate effect.
  - Checked metrics: Pod memory usage + OOMs on node gpu-12.
  - Escalated to infra (Harper) for node investigation.

- 02:45 UTC: infra found a GPU driver crash on gpu-12, kernel logs attached to SRE-487. Rebooted node; some pods rescheduled.
  - Result: cache-service recovered but miss rate remained slightly elevated while pods warm up.

- 03:05 UTC: alert SRE-Medium - inference-worker OOM on batch workers (pod restarts).
  - Root cause: sudden large batched request (long prefix) bypassing batching guard. Need to enforce max-batch-input-size in router.
  - Hotfix: applied soft-limit in routing layer to drop >100k token requests (feature flag on). Reduced OOMs.

Follow-ups / TODOs (priority order):
- P0: Add guard to request-router to reject or chunk extremely long sequences (ticket: SRE-498).
  - Owner: me (Lena). Estimate: 2d dev + 1d rollout + canary.
- P0: Postmortem for cache-service evictions (SRE-487). Draft due by EOD 2026-03-23.
  - Collect kernel logs from gpu-12 (Harper). Attach link in Confluence.
- P1: Add automated node-healthcheck to detect GPU driver instability and cordon nodes automatically. (infra ownership)
- P1: Review and strengthen memory limits for batch workers; consider soft OOM kill metric alert.
- P2: Add a staging test that replays high-length requests to catch router bypass cases. Link to PR#1283.

Runbook notes / edits needed:
- runbooks/cache-service.md:
  - Add troubleshooting step: check kernel/gpu-driver logs and node-level OOMs (we only had app-level steps previously).
  - Add quick rollback steps for cache config change and pod warmup checklist.
- runbooks/inference-worker.md:
  - Add guidance for max-batch-input-size and soft-limit rollout.
  - Add a playbook entry for partial traffic-shed vs full service restart.

Pager details (raw):
- PD incident 86724 - cache-service eviction spike (alerting rule: redis.evictions > 2000/5m) at 02:09 UTC.
- PD incident 86726 - inference-worker OOM (alerting rule: k8s.container.oomburst > 0) at 03:05 UTC.

Quick commands (for reference):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -o wide | grep cache-service
- kubectl logs -n prod <pod> --previous | grep -i oom
- ssh infra@gpu-12 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200' (kernel logs)

Notes to self:
- Remind infra to add gpu driver update notes for 2026-03-20 change. Could be related.
- Check whether scheduled batch job at 02:00 UTC (analytics-replay) might have caused long prefix requests -> tag infra/product.
- Sync with Noah on canary plan before rolling router change.

Retrospective bullets (for postmortem):
- Why did the router allow extremely large requests to the batching pool? missing input size enforcement + feature bypass.
- Why did node-level GPU driver instability surface as application-level evictions? gap in runbook guard (no node-level checks).
- What worked: quick node reboot + soft-limit reduced immediate impact.

Questions / unresolved:
- Harper: can we get driver logs / kernel stack from gpu-12 uploaded to S3? (asked at 04:10 UTC, pending)
- Product: who owns analytics-replay schedule? If it's the cause, need mitigation (throttle or time-shift).

Next steps today:
- 09:00 UTC: 30m post-incident sync with infra + product + eng-serving-runtime (invite Noah, Harper, Arjun).
- Start draft postmortem skeleton in Confluence (link: confluence:postmortems/SRE-487).
- Begin router guard implementation (branch: feat/router-max-input-size).

Misc scratch TODOs (low priority):
- Clean up local notes and upload kernel logs to Confluence.
- Update oncall checklist with node-driver-issue flow.

End of scratchpad.

(Shorthand, will expand in postmortem doc)
